Title: Parcel Bin Packing
Keywords: binary variable, scalar parameter, big-M linking
Description: A shipping company must pack a set of parcels into standard-size boxes for delivery. Each parcel has a known size (volume). All boxes have the same fixed capacity. The company wants to use as few boxes as possible to minimize shipping overhead. Each parcel must be assigned to exactly one box, and no box may be loaded beyond its capacity. A box is considered used if at least one parcel is assigned to it. Determine which parcels go into which box to minimize the total number of boxes used while ensuring every parcel is packed.
Objective: minimize
Objective description: Total number of boxes used across all bin assignments
Decision variables: assign[i,b]: 1 if parcel i is packed into box b, 0 otherwise (binary); use_bin[b]: 1 if box b is used, 0 otherwise (binary)
Parameters: item_size[i]: volume/size of parcel i; bin_capacity: maximum volume capacity of each box (all boxes are identical)
Constraint: Each parcel must be assigned to exactly one box
Constraint: The total size of all parcels assigned to a box must not exceed the box's capacity, and the box must be marked as used if any parcel is assigned to it (bin activation linking)

Title: Multi-Period Capacity Expansion
Keywords: binary variable, ordered set, temporal lag, init constraint, big-M linking
Description: A manufacturer operates two plants and must decide in each period whether to invest in expanding a plant's capacity (binary decision). Capacity accumulates over time: once expanded, the added capacity persists. Production from each plant is limited by its current cumulative capacity. Total production must meet growing demand each period. Minimise total expansion and production costs.
Objective: minimize
Objective description: Total expansion investment plus production costs over all periods
Decision variables: expand[Facilities,Periods]: 1 if plant f is expanded in period t (binary); capacity[Facilities,Periods]: cumulative production capacity of plant f in period t (continuous); produce[Facilities,Periods]: units produced at plant f in period t (continuous)
Parameters: initial_cap[Facilities]: starting capacity before any expansions; expansion_size[Facilities]: capacity added per expansion event; expansion_cost[Facilities]: capital cost per expansion; demand[Periods]: total demand that must be met each period; prod_cost[Facilities]: variable production cost per unit
Constraint: Capacity initialisation: first-period capacity = initial_cap + expansion if expanded in p1
Constraint: Capacity update (temporal lag): each period's capacity = previous capacity + new expansion
Constraint: Production upper bound: production cannot exceed current period capacity
Constraint: Demand satisfaction: total production across plants meets demand each period

Description: A company is evaluating a set of investment projects. Each project has a known net present value (NPV) if undertaken. Undertaking a project requires capital expenditures spread across multiple time periods — the expenditure required for each project in each period is known. In each period, the total capital expenditure across all selected projects cannot exceed a period-specific budget limit. Projects are binary decisions: either fully undertaken or not at all. Determine which projects to select to maximize total NPV subject to the per-period budget constraints.
Objective: maximize
Objective description: Total net present value (NPV) of all selected investment projects
Decision variables: select[p]: 1 if project p is selected for investment, 0 otherwise (binary)
Parameters: npv[p]: net present value of project p if selected; investment_required[p,t]: capital expenditure required by project p in period t; budget[t]: maximum capital available for investment in period t
Constraint: For each time period, the total capital expenditure required by all selected projects must not exceed the period's available budget

Title: Cross-Docking Distribution Network
Keywords: 
Description: A distributor ships products from several plants to customers via distribution centers (DCs). Unlike a standard warehouse, each DC operates as a cross-dock: all units received must be immediately re-shipped to customers in the same period — no inventory is held at the DC. Plants have limited supply capacity. Customer demand must be met exactly. Determine the shipment volumes on each plant-to-DC and DC-to-customer lane to minimize total shipping cost.
Objective: minimize
Objective description: Total shipping cost = sum of per-unit costs on plant-to-DC and DC-to-customer lanes
Decision variables: ship_in[p,d]: units shipped from plant p to DC d (continuous, non-negative); ship_out[d,c]: units shipped from DC d to customer c (continuous, non-negative)

Constraint: Cross-dock balance: total inbound flow to each DC equals total outbound flow (no storage)
Constraint: Plant capacity: total outbound shipments from each plant cannot exceed its supply capacity
Constraint: Demand coverage: total inbound shipments to each customer must exactly meet that customer's demand

Constraint: Charge rate limit: charge[t] <= max_charge_rate
Constraint: Discharge rate limit: discharge[t] <= max_discharge_rate
Constraint: Capacity limit: SOC[t] <= capacity

Title: Capacitated Facility Location
Keywords: binary variable, domain filter, big-M linking
Description: A retailer is deciding which distribution facilities to open in order to serve a set of customers. There are several candidate facility locations, each with a known fixed opening cost and a maximum throughput capacity. For each facility-customer pair there is a known per-unit shipping cost. Each customer has a known demand that must be fully served. A facility can only ship to customers if it is open, and its total shipments across all customers cannot exceed its throughput capacity. An open facility may serve any customer, but a closed facility may ship nothing. Choose which facilities to open and how much to ship from each to each customer to minimize total fixed opening costs plus variable shipping costs.
Objective: minimize
Objective description: Total cost = fixed opening costs for opened facilities plus per-unit shipping costs times quantities shipped, summed over all facility-customer pairs
Decision variables: open_fac[f]: 1 if facility f is opened, 0 otherwise (binary); assign[f,c]: units shipped from facility f to customer c (continuous, non-negative)
Parameters: fixed_cost[f]: one-time fixed cost to open facility f; facility_capacity[f]: maximum total units facility f can ship across all customers; serve_cost[f,c]: per-unit shipping cost from facility f to customer c; demand[c]: units demanded by customer c that must be exactly fulfilled
Constraint: For each customer, total shipments received from all facilities must exactly equal the customer's demand
Constraint: For each facility, total shipments to all customers must not exceed the facility's throughput capacity if it is open, or zero if it is closed (big-M linking)
Constraint: For each facility-customer pair, the amount shipped cannot exceed the customer's demand times whether the facility is open (prevents any flow from a closed facility)

Title: Financial Cash Flow Management
Keywords: ordered set, temporal lag, init constraint, scalar parameter, multi-variable temporal balance
Description: A company plans borrowing and investment decisions over 8 months. Each month has a known net operating cash flow. The company can borrow short-term at an interest rate or invest surplus cash at a return rate. It must maintain a minimum cash balance each month and stay within a maximum loan limit. Minimize total net interest cost (borrowing cost minus investment return).
Objective: minimize
Objective description: Total net interest cost = sum over months of (borrow_rate * loan_balance - invest_rate * invest_balance). Investment balance is capped at max_invest to keep the model bounded.
Decision variables: borrow[Months]: short-term borrowing in month t (continuous, non-negative); repay[Months]: loan repayment in month t (continuous, non-negative); invest[Months]: surplus investment in month t (continuous, non-negative); withdraw[Months]: investment withdrawal in month t (continuous, non-negative); loan_balance[Months]: outstanding loan at end of month t (continuous, non-negative); invest_balance[Months]: investment portfolio at end of month t (continuous, non-negative)
Parameters: net_cash[Months]: operating cash flow each month (can be negative); borrow_rate: monthly interest rate on loans (scalar); invest_rate: monthly return on investments (scalar); max_loan: maximum outstanding loan balance (scalar); min_cash: minimum required cash balance each month (scalar); max_invest: maximum investment portfolio balance each month (scalar)
Constraint: loan_balance_update_init: first-month loan balance equals new borrowing minus repayment
Constraint: loan_balance_update: each month's loan balance equals previous balance plus new borrowing minus repayment (temporal lag)
Constraint: invest_balance_update_init: first-month investment balance equals new investment minus withdrawals
Constraint: invest_balance_update: each month's investment balance equals previous balance plus new investment minus withdrawals (temporal lag)
Constraint: cash_flow_balance: operating cash flow plus borrowing minus repayment plus withdrawals minus investment must meet minimum cash requirement
Constraint: max_loan_limit: outstanding loan balance must not exceed maximum loan limit
Constraint: max_invest_limit: investment portfolio balance must not exceed maximum investment limit

Description: A manufacturer wants to produce as close to demand as possible for each product. Due to capacity limits, some products cannot meet demand. Title: Hub-and-Spoke Network Location
Keywords: binary variable, big-M linking, exclude_diagonal, duplicate set domain, aliased indexed_sum, sparse parameter
Description: A logistics company routes shipments from origins to destinations through a hub-and-spoke network. It must decide which of 3 candidate hubs to open (fixed cost). Shipments from each origin are consolidated at one hub, then possibly transferred to another hub before being delivered to destinations. Each hub has a throughput capacity. Minimize total fixed plus transportation costs.
Objective: minimize
Objective description: Total cost = hub opening costs + collection costs (origin to hub) + transfer costs (hub to hub) + delivery costs (hub to destination)

Constraint: supply_dispatch: all supply from each origin must be sent to hubs
Constraint: demand_fulfillment: all demand at each destination must be received from hubs
Constraint: hub_flow_balance: at each hub, inflow (from origins + other hubs) equals outflow (to destinations + other hubs)
Constraint: collect_big_m: collection from origin to hub is zero if hub is not open
Constraint: deliver_big_m: delivery from hub to destination is zero if hub is not open
Constraint: hub_capacity_limit: total flow through a hub (inbound) cannot exceed its capacity times its open indicator
Constraint: transfer_big_m: inter-hub transfer is zero if the originating hub is not open

Title: Single-Product Inventory Planning with Demand Backlogging
Keywords: ordered set, temporal lag, init constraint, scalar parameter, deviation variables
Description: A retailer manages a single product over a multi-period planning horizon. In each period the retailer may place an order (up to a maximum order size) to replenish stock. Demand is known but may exceed the available supply in some periods; unmet demand is backlogged at a per-unit penalty cost and carried forward to be satisfied in a later period. On-hand inventory earns a holding cost. The goal is to determine order quantities that minimize total ordering, holding, and backlog penalty costs while respecting the order size limit.
Objective: minimize

Title: Open Shop Scheduling — Minimize Makespan
Keywords: scalar variable, binary variable, big-M linking, duplicate set domain, exclude_diagonal
Description: Four jobs must each be processed on three machines. Each job-machine combination has a known processing time. On each machine, jobs are processed one at a time (no overlap). Objective description: Makespan: the time by which all jobs have finished on all machines
Decision variables: start[Jobs,Machines]: start time of job j on machine m (continuous, non-negative); before[Jobs,Jobs,Machines]: 1 if job i is processed before job j on machine m (binary, exclude diagonal); makespan: overall completion time (scalar continuous)
Parameters: proc_time[Jobs,Machines]: processing time of job j on machine m; big_m: large constant for disjunctive big-M constraints (scalar)
Constraint: no_overlap_fwd: if job i precedes job j on machine m (before[i,j,m]=1), then job j cannot start until job i finishes
Constraint: no_overlap_rev: if job j precedes job i on machine m (before[i,j,m]=0), then job i cannot start until job j finishes
Constraint: makespan_bound: makespan >= start[j,m] + proc_time[j,m] for all jobs and machines

Title: Capacitated Lot Sizing Problem (CLSP)
Keywords: binary variable, ordered set, temporal lag, init constraint, scalar parameter, big-M linking
Description: A manufacturer produces several products on a shared machine over a multi-period planning horizon. In each period, a product can only be produced if the machine is set up for it, incurring a fixed setup cost. Variable production cost and per-unit holding cost also apply. The machine has a limited total capacity per period shared across all products. Known demand must be met each period from available inventory. Determine which products to set up and how much to produce each period to minimize total setup, production, and holding costs.
Objective: minimize
Objective description: Total cost = sum of setup costs (when machine is set up for a product) plus variable production costs plus inventory holding costs, over all products and periods
Decision variables: produce[p,t]: units of product p produced in period t (continuous, non-negative); setup[p,t]: 1 if product p is set up on the machine in period t, else 0 (binary); inventory[p,t]: units of product p in inventory at the end of period t (continuous, non-negative)

Constraint: Inventory balance initialization: first-period ending inventory equals initial inventory plus production minus demand
Constraint: Inventory balance: ending inventory equals previous inventory plus production minus demand (temporal lag)
Constraint: Setup link: production quantity is zero unless the machine is set up (big-M linking constraint)
Constraint: Machine capacity: total production across all products in a period must not exceed the machine capacity

Title: Make-or-Buy Sourcing Decision
Keywords: binary variable, scalar parameter, big-M linking
Description: A manufacturer must decide, for each product, whether to produce it in-house or purchase it from an external supplier. Constraint: Labor capacity: total production across all products must not exceed available labor capacity

Title: Multi-Period Production-Inventory-Distribution Network
Keywords: domain filter, sparse filter, ordered set, temporal lag, init constraint
Description: A manufacturer operates a three-tier distribution network — plants, warehouses, and retailers — over multiple time periods. At each plant, a manager decides how many units to produce each period subject to a per-period production capacity. Produced goods add to plant inventory; a per-unit holding cost is charged for every unit stored at a plant at each period end. From each plant, goods are shipped to warehouses over established lanes (a sparse arc set), each with a per-unit shipping cost and a per-period throughput capacity. Warehouses carry inventory across periods at a per-unit holding cost and are limited by a storage capacity constraint. From each warehouse, goods are forwarded to retailers over another sparse set of established lanes, each with a per-unit shipping cost and a per-period arc capacity. Each retailer has a deterministic demand per period that must be exactly fulfilled. The goal is to choose production quantities, inter-tier shipments, and ending inventory levels at each plant and warehouse to minimize total cost: production costs, plant and warehouse holding costs, and transportation costs across all arcs and periods.
Objective: minimize
Objective description: Total cost: production costs at plants, inventory holding costs at plants and warehouses, and per-unit shipping costs on all plant-to-warehouse and warehouse-to-retailer arcs, summed across all valid arcs and periods
Decision variables: produce[i,t]: units produced at plant i in period t (continuous, non-negative); inventory_plant[i,t]: inventory held at plant i at end of period t (continuous, non-negative); inventory_wh[w,t]: inventory held at warehouse w at end of period t (continuous, non-negative); flow_pw[i,w,t]: units shipped from plant i to warehouse w in period t (continuous, non-negative, defined only for valid arcs); flow_wr[w,r,t]: units shipped from warehouse w to retailer r in period t (continuous, non-negative, defined only for valid arcs)
Parameters: prod_cost[i]: production cost per unit at plant i; prod_capacity[i]: maximum units that can be produced at plant i in any single period; hold_cost_plant[i]: inventory holding cost per unit per period at plant i; initial_inv_plant[i]: inventory held at plant i at the start of the planning horizon (before period t0); hold_cost_wh[w]: inventory holding cost per unit per period at warehouse w; wh_capacity[w]: maximum inventory units that can be stored at warehouse w at the end of any period; initial_inv_wh[w]: inventory held at warehouse w at the start of the planning horizon; demand[r,t]: units required by retailer r in period t, which must be exactly fulfilled; cost_pw[i,w]: per-unit shipping cost from plant i to warehouse w (defined only for valid arcs); cost_wr[w,r]: per-unit shipping cost from warehouse w to retailer r (defined only for valid arcs); cap_pw[i,w]: maximum units shippable from plant i to warehouse w in a single period (defined only for valid arcs); cap_wr[w,r]: maximum units shippable from warehouse w to retailer r in a single period (defined only for valid arcs)
Constraint: Plant inventory balance for the first period: ending inventory at plant i equals initial inventory plus production minus total shipments out to warehouses in period t0
Constraint: Plant inventory balance for subsequent periods: ending inventory at plant i in period t equals ending inventory in the previous period plus production minus total shipments out to warehouses
Constraint: Warehouse inventory balance for the first period: ending inventory at warehouse w equals initial inventory plus total inflow from plants minus total outflow to retailers in period t0
Constraint: Warehouse inventory balance for subsequent periods: ending inventory at warehouse w in period t equals ending inventory in the previous period plus total inflow from plants minus total outflow to retailers
Constraint: Production at each plant in each period must not exceed the plant's per-period production capacity
Constraint: Inventory held at each warehouse at the end of each period must not exceed the warehouse's storage capacity
Constraint: For each retailer and period, total inflow from all connected warehouses must exactly equal the retailer's demand
Constraint: Flow on each plant-to-warehouse arc in each period must not exceed that arc's per-period throughput capacity
Constraint: Flow on each warehouse-to-retailer arc in each period must not exceed that arc's per-period throughput capacity

Title: Multi-Period Production-Inventory-Distribution Network with Plant Opening, Closing, and Step Operating Costs
Keywords: binary variable, domain filter, sparse filter, ordered set, temporal lag, init constraint, big-M linking, step cost
Description: A manufacturer operates a three-tier distribution network — plants, warehouses, and retailers — over multiple time periods. Each plant starts the horizon in a known initial state (open or closed). In each period, each plant is either open or closed. A plant may be opened or closed any number of times within the horizon. Opening a plant (transitioning from closed to open) incurs a one-time opening cost in that period. Closing a plant (transitioning from open to closed) incurs a one-time closing cost in that period. When a plant is open it incurs a per-period step operating cost that depends on its production tier (low, medium, or high), each tier covering a range of output levels. When a plant is closed it incurs no operating cost and cannot produce. In each period, each open plant selects exactly one tier; closed plants select no tier. Within the selected tier, the actual production quantity can range freely between the tier's lower and upper bounds, and each unit also incurs a per-unit production cost. Produced goods enter plant inventory; a holding cost applies to every unit stored at a plant at period end. Goods are shipped from plants to warehouses and from warehouses to retailers over a sparse set of established arcs, each with a per-unit shipping cost and a per-period arc capacity. Warehouses hold inventory across periods at a holding cost and are limited by a storage capacity. Each retailer has a known demand per period that must be exactly met. The goal is to decide when to open and close each plant, which tier each open plant uses each period, how much to produce, and how to route goods to minimise total cost: plant opening costs, plant closing costs, step operating costs, per-unit production costs, plant and warehouse holding costs, and transportation costs.

Description: A manufacturer operates a three-tier distribution network — plants, warehouses, and retailers — over multiple time periods. At each plant, a manager decides how many units to produce each period subject to a per-period production capacity. Produced goods add to plant inventory; a per-unit holding cost is charged for every unit stored at a plant at each period end. From each plant, goods are shipped to warehouses over established lanes (a sparse arc set). Each arc offers quantity-discount pricing: the per-unit shipping cost decreases as the shipment volume moves into higher volume tiers, and each shipment dispatched on an arc incurs a fixed charge. An arc has a fixed shipment size (e.g. truck capacity), so the number of dispatches required in a period equals the ceiling of total flow divided by shipment size. Total fixed cost for an arc in a period is therefore fixed_cost_per_shipment times the number of shipments. Warehouses carry inventory across periods at a per-unit holding cost and are limited by a storage capacity constraint. From each warehouse, goods are forwarded to retailers over another sparse set of established lanes, each with the same tier-based pricing and multi-shipment fixed-charge structure. Each retailer has a deterministic demand per period that must be exactly fulfilled. The goal is to choose production quantities, inter-tier shipments, tier selections, shipment counts, and ending inventory levels to minimize total cost: production costs, plant and warehouse holding costs, variable tier-based shipping costs on all arcs, and total fixed shipment charges across all arcs and periods.

problem.title: Multi-Period Production-Inventory-Distribution Network with Step Transportation Cost and Fixed Shipment Charge
problem.description: A manufacturer operates a three-tier distribution network — plants, warehouses, and retailers — over multiple time periods. At each plant, a manager decides how many units to produce each period subject to a per-period production capacity. Produced goods add to plant inventory; a per-unit holding cost is charged for every unit stored at a plant at each period end. From each plant, goods are shipped to warehouses over established lanes (a sparse arc set). Each arc offers quantity-discount pricing: the per-unit shipping cost decreases as the shipment volume moves into higher volume tiers, and each shipment dispatched on an arc incurs a fixed charge. An arc has a fixed shipment size (e.g. truck capacity), so the number of dispatches required in a period equals the ceiling of total flow divided by shipment size. Total fixed cost for an arc in a period is therefore fixed_cost_per_shipment times the number of shipments. Warehouses carry inventory across periods at a per-unit holding cost and are limited by a storage capacity constraint. From each warehouse, goods are forwarded to retailers over another sparse set of established lanes, each with the same tier-based pricing and multi-shipment fixed-charge structure. Each retailer has a deterministic demand per period that must be exactly fulfilled. The goal is to choose production quantities, inter-tier shipments, tier selections, shipment counts, and ending inventory levels to minimize total cost: production costs, plant and warehouse holding costs, variable tier-based shipping costs on all arcs, and total fixed shipment charges across all arcs and periods.

Total fixed cost for an arc is fixed_cost_per_dispatch * num_shipments. The tier selection constraint (flow_pw_tier_select) restricts at most one pricing tier to be active per arc per period, ensuring volume-based pricing is applied to the total flow rather than allowing simultaneous tier mixing. Combining tier-specific per-unit costs with flow tier variables linearizes what would otherwise be a nonlinear quantity-discount cost function.

Title: Three-Tier Distribution Network Flow
Keywords: domain filter, sparse filter
Description: A logistics company operates a three-tier distribution network: manufacturing plants ship goods to regional warehouses, which then forward them to end retailers. Each plant has a maximum supply capacity. Each retailer has a fixed demand that must be exactly met. Arcs between tiers have both a per-unit shipping cost and a throughput capacity limit. Not all plant-warehouse and warehouse-retailer pairs have established shipping lanes — only arcs present in the cost tables are valid. Flow must be conserved at each warehouse: total inflow from plants must equal total outflow to retailers. Find the minimum-cost flow plan that satisfies all retailer demands without violating any arc or plant capacity.
Objective: minimize
Objective description: Total shipping cost across all plant-to-warehouse and warehouse-to-retailer arcs, weighted by flow volume on each arc
Decision variables: flow_pw[i,w]: units shipped from plant i to warehouse w (continuous, non-negative, defined only for valid arcs); flow_wr[w,r]: units shipped from warehouse w to retailer r (continuous, non-negative, defined only for valid arcs)
Parameters: supply[i]: maximum supply available at plant i; demand[r]: demand that must be exactly fulfilled at retailer r; cost_pw[i,w]: per-unit shipping cost from plant i to warehouse w (defined only for valid arcs); cost_wr[w,r]: per-unit shipping cost from warehouse w to retailer r (defined only for valid arcs); cap_pw[i,w]: maximum throughput capacity on the arc from plant i to warehouse w (defined only for valid arcs); cap_wr[w,r]: maximum throughput capacity on the arc from warehouse w to retailer r (defined only for valid arcs)
Constraint: Total flow shipped out of each plant across all outgoing arcs must not exceed that plant's supply capacity
Constraint: Total flow received by each retailer across all incoming arcs must exactly equal that retailer's demand
Constraint: For each warehouse, total flow arriving from all plants must equal total flow departing to all retailers (flow conservation)
Constraint: Flow on each plant-to-warehouse arc must not exceed that arc's capacity
Constraint: Flow on each warehouse-to-retailer arc must not exceed that arc's capacity

Title: Perishable Inventory Planning with Expiry Waste
Keywords: ordered set, temporal lag, init constraint
Description: A retailer manages several perishable products (e.g., fresh food) over a daily planning horizon. Purchased goods can be held for at most one period before they expire; any unsold inventory from the previous period must be wasted. Demand must be satisfied each day. The retailer incurs a purchase cost per unit bought, a holding cost per unit carried overnight (end-of-period inventory), and a waste penalty per unit discarded. Determine daily purchase quantities to minimize total cost while ensuring demand is met and no inventory is held past its shelf life.
Objective: minimize
Objective description: Total cost = purchase cost + holding cost for overnight inventory + waste penalty for expired units, summed over all products and periods
Decision variables: purchase[p,t]: units of product p purchased in period t (continuous, non-negative); inventory[p,t]: units of product p in storage at end of period t (continuous, non-negative); waste[p,t]: units of product p expired/wasted in period t (continuous, non-negative)
Parameters: demand[p,t]: demand for product p in period t; purchase_cost[p]: cost per unit purchased for product p; holding_cost[p]: cost per unit held overnight for product p; waste_penalty[p]: penalty per unit wasted/expired for product p; initial_inventory[p]: units of product p on hand at the start of the planning horizon (age 1, will expire in period 1 if not used); storage_cap[p]: maximum units of product p that can be stored overnight
Constraint: Balance initialization: first-period inventory plus waste plus demand equals initial inventory plus purchases
Constraint: Balance: current inventory plus waste plus demand equals previous inventory plus purchases (temporal lag)
Constraint: Expiry (shelf-life = 1 period): end-of-period inventory cannot exceed units purchased in that period — forcing old stock to be wasted
Constraint: Storage capacity: end-of-period inventory for each product must not exceed the storage limit

Title: Furniture Factory Multi-Week Production Mix
Keywords: binary variable, integer variable, scalar parameter, big-M linking
Description: A furniture factory produces chairs, tables, and shelves over a multi-week planning horizon. Each product type requires a certain number of labor-hours and board-feet of wood per unit. The factory has a fixed weekly supply of labor hours and wood. Products can only be produced in whole units — no fractional quantities. If the factory decides to include a product type in a given week's production run, it incurs a fixed setup cost and a variable per unit production cost, and the factory must produce at least a minimum batch size for that product type for this week. Each product type also has a maximum weekly production capacity due to machine constraints. Due to changeover constraints, at most two product types can be produced in any given week. Each product type has a revenue per unit produced. Determine which product types to include in the production plan each week and how many units of each to make to maximize total revenue minus total cost across all weeks.
Objective: maximize
Objective description: Total revenue from production minus total cost (fixed setup cost plus variable per unit production cost) summed across all weeks
Decision variables: produce[p,w]: integer number of units of product p to produce in week w; active[p,w]: binary, 1 if product p is included in week w's production run, 0 otherwise

Constraint: Total labor-hours consumed by all active product types in week w cannot exceed the factory's fixed weekly labor capacity
Constraint: Total board-feet of wood consumed by all active product types in week w cannot exceed the factory's fixed weekly wood supply
Constraint: If product type p is included in week w's production run, at least min_batch[p] units must be produced that week; if not included, production must be zero
Constraint: Production of product type p in week w cannot exceed its maximum weekly machine capacity, and production can only be positive if product type p is active in that week
Constraint: Due to changeover constraints, at most two product types can be active in any given week

Title: Bill-of-Materials Production Planning with Alternative BOMs
Keywords: BOM parameter
Description: A factory produces a set of finished products. Each finished product can be assembled using one or more alternative Bill of Materials (BOM) configurations. Producing one unit of product p using BOM b requires a known quantity of each component c as specified by that BOM. Different BOMs for the same product may use different components or different quantities, for example substituting one raw material for another. Constraint: In the first period, workforce equals initial workforce plus hires minus fires
Constraint: In each subsequent period, workforce equals previous period workforce plus hires minus fires
Constraint: Workforce in each period must meet or exceed the required staffing level
Constraint: Workforce in each period must not exceed the maximum allowed headcount

Title: Single-Source Supplier Selection
Keywords: binary variable, domain filter, big-M linking
Description: A manufacturer must source raw materials for a set of factories from a set of approved suppliers. Due to a quality-control policy, each factory must source all of its material from exactly one supplier — split orders across multiple suppliers are not allowed. Each supplier has a total supply capacity that limits the total quantity it can ship to all factories. The unit sourcing cost from each supplier to each factory is known. Choose which supplier serves each factory and how much is shipped to minimize total sourcing cost, while satisfying all factory demands, respecting supplier capacities, and enforcing the single-source assignment rule.
Objective: minimize
Objective description: Total sourcing cost = sum of per-unit costs times quantities shipped, over all supplier-factory pairs

Constraint: For each factory, total material received from all suppliers must exactly equal the factory's demand
Constraint: For each supplier, total quantity shipped to all factories must not exceed the supplier's capacity
Constraint: For each supplier-factory pair, quantity shipped cannot exceed the factory's demand times whether that supplier is assigned to that factory (big-M flow linking: no flow from an unassigned supplier)

Title: Multi-Product Multi-Period Regional Distribution
Keywords: domain filter
Description: A regional distribution company ships two product types (Product A and Product B) from three warehouses to four retail customers over three time periods. Due to geographic constraints, only eight of the twelve possible warehouse-customer routes have established shipping lanes, and the same set of routes is used for all products and periods. Each route has a fixed per-unit shipping cost that does not vary by product or period. Each warehouse has a known supply capacity for each product in each period. Each customer has a fixed demand for each product in each period that must be exactly fulfilled. Determine how much of each product to ship along each available route in each period to fulfill all customer demands without exceeding warehouse supplies, at minimum total shipping cost.
Objective: minimize
Objective description: Total shipping cost summed over all valid routes, products, and periods, weighted by the amount shipped
Decision variables: ship[w,c,p,t]: amount of product p shipped from warehouse w to customer c in period t (continuous, non-negative, defined only for valid warehouse-customer routes)
Parameters: transport_cost[w,c]: cost per unit shipped from warehouse w to customer c, shared across all products and periods (defined only for the subset of valid routes); supply[w,p,t]: supply of product p available at warehouse w in period t; demand[c,p,t]: demand for product p required by customer c in period t, which must be exactly met
Constraint: For each warehouse, product, and period, the total amount of that product shipped out across all valid routes must not exceed the warehouse's supply of that product in that period
Constraint: For each customer, product, and period, the total amount of that product shipped in from any warehouse via valid routes must exactly equal the customer's demand for that product in that period

Title: Multi-Product Multi-Period Transportation with Route-Level and Site-Level Flow Allocation
Keywords: domain filter, duplicate set
Description: A regional distribution company ships two product types (Product A and Product B) from three warehouses to four retail customers over three time periods. Only eight of the twelve possible warehouse-customer routes have established shipping lanes. Each route has a fixed per-unit shipping cost shared across all products and periods. Each warehouse has a known supply capacity for each product in each period. Each customer has a fixed demand for each product in each period that must be exactly fulfilled. Additionally, certain routes are subject to flow allocation constraints: the total flow on a given route from a warehouse (summed over products) must be at least a specified percentage of the total flow on another route from the same warehouse. Similarly, certain warehouse pairs are subject to site-level flow allocation constraints: the total flow through one warehouse (summed over all routes, products, and in each period) must be at least a specified percentage of the total flow through another warehouse in that period. Determine how much of each product to ship along each valid route in each period to fulfill all customer demands without exceeding warehouse supplies, while satisfying all route-level and site-level flow allocation requirements, at minimum total shipping cost.
Objective: minimize
Objective description: Total shipping cost summed over all valid routes, products, and periods, weighted by the amount shipped
Decision variables: ship[w,c,p,t]: amount of product p shipped from warehouse w to customer c in period t (continuous, non-negative, defined only for valid warehouse-customer routes)
Parameters: transport_cost[w,c]: cost per unit shipped from warehouse w to customer c, shared across all products and periods (defined only for the subset of valid routes); supply[w,p,t]: supply of product p available at warehouse w in period t; demand[c,p,t]: demand for product p required by customer c in period t, which must be exactly met; min_route_share_pct[w,c1,c2]: minimum fraction such that total flow from warehouse w to customer c1 must be at least this fraction of total flow from warehouse w to customer c2 (sparse: defined only for constrained route pairs); min_site_share_pct[w1,w2]: minimum fraction such that total flow through warehouse w1 must be at least this fraction of total flow through warehouse w2 per period (sparse: defined only for constrained warehouse pairs)
Constraint: For each warehouse, product, and period, the total amount of that product shipped out across all valid routes must not exceed the warehouse's supply of that product in that period
Constraint: For each customer, product, and period, the total amount of that product shipped in from any warehouse via valid routes must exactly equal the customer's demand for that product in that period
Constraint: For each (warehouse, primary-customer, reference-customer, period) tuple listed in the route allocation table, the total flow (summed over products) shipped from the warehouse to the primary customer must be at least a specified percentage of the total flow shipped from the same warehouse to the reference customer in that period; trivially satisfied (0 >= 0) for all other combinations
Constraint: For each (warehouse1, warehouse2, period) tuple listed in the site allocation table, the total flow (summed over all customers and products) shipped out of warehouse1 must be at least a specified percentage of the total flow shipped out of warehouse2 in that period; trivially satisfied for all other combinations

Title: Multi-Product Multi-Period Transportation with Flow Capacity and Route Activation
Keywords: binary variable, domain filter, sparse filter, big-M linking
Description: A regional distribution company ships two product types (Product A and Product B) from three warehouses to four retail customers over three time periods. Only eight of the twelve possible warehouse-customer routes have established shipping lanes. Each route has a fixed per-unit shipping cost shared across all products and periods. Each route also has a maximum throughput capacity per product per period — the amount of a given product that can be shipped on a given route in a given period is bounded. A route may only carry shipments in a period if it is explicitly activated for that period; activating a route is a binary decision. Due to operational constraints, at most six routes may be simultaneously active in any given period. Each warehouse has a known supply capacity for each product in each period. Each customer has a fixed demand for each product in each period that must be exactly fulfilled. Determine which routes to activate each period and how much of each product to ship along each active route to fulfill all customer demands without exceeding warehouse supplies or route throughput capacities, while keeping active routes per period at most six, at minimum total shipping cost.
Objective: minimize
Objective description: Total shipping cost summed over all valid routes, products, and periods, weighted by the amount shipped
Decision variables: ship[w,c,p,t]: amount of product p shipped from warehouse w to customer c in period t (continuous, non-negative, defined only for valid warehouse-customer routes); active_route[w,c,t]: 1 if the route from warehouse w to customer c is activated in period t, 0 otherwise (binary, defined only for valid routes)
Parameters: transport_cost[w,c]: cost per unit shipped from warehouse w to customer c, shared across all products and periods (defined only for the subset of valid routes); supply[w,p,t]: supply of product p available at warehouse w in period t; demand[c,p,t]: demand for product p required by customer c in period t, which must be exactly met; route_capacity[w,c,p]: maximum units of product p that can be shipped from warehouse w to customer c in any single period (defined only for valid routes)
Constraint: For each warehouse, product, and period, the total amount of that product shipped out across all valid routes must not exceed the warehouse's supply of that product in that period
Constraint: For each customer, product, and period, the total amount of that product shipped in from any warehouse via valid routes must exactly equal the customer's demand for that product in that period
Constraint: For each valid route, product, and period, the amount shipped cannot exceed the route's throughput capacity for that product multiplied by whether the route is active in that period (big-M linking constraint)
Constraint: For each period, the total number of active routes across all valid warehouse-customer pairs must not exceed six

Title: Multi-Product Multi-Period Transportation with Truck Type Selection
Keywords: integer variable, domain filter, sparse filter
Description: A regional distribution company ships two product types (Product A and Product B) from three warehouses to four retail customers over three time periods. Due to geographic constraints, only eight of the twelve possible warehouse-customer routes have established shipping lanes. Each route has a fixed per-unit shipping cost shared across all products and periods. In addition, all shipments must be transported in discrete trucks. Three truck types are available (small, medium, large), each with a different cargo capacity (maximum total units carried per trip) and a fixed dispatch cost charged per truck used, regardless of how full it is. For each warehouse-customer route in each period, the company chooses how many trucks of each type to dispatch. The total cargo capacity of dispatched trucks on a route must cover the total volume of all products shipped on that route in that period. Each warehouse has a known supply of each product each period. Each customer has a fixed demand for each product each period that must be exactly fulfilled. Minimize total cost: per-unit shipping costs across all products and periods, plus fixed dispatch costs for all trucks used.
Objective: minimize
Objective description: Total cost: per-unit shipping costs summed over all valid routes, products, and periods, plus fixed dispatch costs summed over all valid routes, truck types, and periods
Decision variables: ship[i,j,p,t]: amount of product p shipped from warehouse i to customer j in period t (continuous, non-negative, defined only for valid routes); trucks[i,j,k,t]: number of trucks of type k dispatched from warehouse i to customer j in period t (integer, non-negative, defined only for valid routes)
Parameters: transport_cost[i,j]: per-unit shipping cost from warehouse i to customer j, shared across all products and periods (defined only for valid routes); supply[i,p,t]: supply of product p available at warehouse i in period t; demand[j,p,t]: demand for product p required by customer j in period t, which must be exactly met; truck_size[k]: cargo capacity in units for one truck of type k (maximum total units that one truck can carry per trip); truck_fixed_cost[k]: fixed dispatch cost per truck of type k used on any route in any period
Constraint: For each warehouse, product, and period, the total amount shipped out across all valid routes must not exceed the warehouse's available supply
Constraint: For each customer, product, and period, the total amount received from all warehouses via valid routes must exactly equal the customer's demand
Constraint: For each valid route and period, the total volume shipped across all products must not exceed the combined cargo capacity of all trucks dispatched on that route in that period

Title: Unit Commitment Problem
Keywords: binary variable, ordered set, temporal lag, init constraint, big-M linking, scalar parameter
Description: A power system operator schedules three generators over 8 hours. Each generator has minimum and maximum output limits, a fuel cost per MWh, and a startup cost when brought online. A binary commit variable determines if a generator is online each hour. Generation is only possible when committed (big-M linking). A binary startup variable captures when a generator transitions from off to on. Power balance must be met each hour. Minimize total fuel plus startup costs.
Objective: minimize
Objective description: Total cost = sum of fuel costs (fuel_cost[g]*generate[g,t]) plus startup costs (startup_cost[g]*startup[g,t]) over all generators and hours
Decision variables: commit[g,t]: 1 if generator g is online in hour t (binary); generate[g,t]: MW output of generator g in hour t (continuous, non-negative); startup[g,t]: 1 if generator g starts up at hour t (binary)
Parameters: fuel_cost[g]: cost per MWh for generator g; startup_cost[g]: fixed cost when generator g starts up; min_output[g]: minimum MW output when generator g is online; max_output[g]: maximum MW output when generator g is online; demand[t]: MW demand in hour t
Constraint: Power balance: total generation equals demand each hour
Constraint: Minimum generation: when committed, generate at least min_output (big-M lower bound)
Constraint: Maximum generation: when committed, generate at most max_output (big-M upper bound)
Constraint: Startup link init: startup[g,h1] >= commit[g,h1] (first period, no previous state)
Constraint: Startup link: startup[g,t] >= commit[g,t] - commit[g,t-1] for subsequent periods (temporal lag)

examples.text:
Title: Capacitated Vehicle Routing Problem (CVRP) with MTZ Subtour Elimination
Keywords: binary variable, integer variable, exclude diagonal, upper bound set, init constraint, set size expression, duplicate set, scalar parameter
Description: A delivery company must route a fleet of vehicles from a central depot to serve a set of customers, then return to the depot. Each customer has a known demand. Each vehicle has a fixed load capacity — the total demand of all customers on a vehicle's route cannot exceed its capacity. The travel distance (cost) between every pair of locations (depot and customers) is known. Each customer must be visited exactly once by exactly one vehicle. Subtour elimination is enforced via Miller-Tucker-Zemlin (MTZ) constraints using integer position variables. Find the set of routes — one per vehicle — that minimizes total travel distance while serving all customers within vehicle capacity.
Objective: minimize
Objective description: Total travel distance across all activated arcs (vehicle routes), summed over all vehicle-arc combinations
Decision variables: y[l1,l2,v]: 1 if vehicle v travels directly from location l1 to location l2, 0 otherwise (binary, self-loops excluded); u[c,v]: visit position of customer c in vehicle v's route, used for MTZ subtour elimination (integer, lower bound 1)
Parameters: distance[l1,l2]: travel distance from location l1 to location l2; demand[c]: units of goods required by customer c; vehicle_capacity: maximum load each vehicle can carry (uniform across all vehicles)
Constraint: Each customer must be visited exactly once across all vehicles and all incoming arcs
Constraint: For each location and vehicle, the number of arcs entering that location equals the number leaving (flow conservation)
Constraint: Each vehicle departs the depot at most once (depot departure)
Constraint: Each vehicle returns to the depot at most once (depot return)
Constraint: For each vehicle, the total demand of all customers visited must not exceed the vehicle's load capacity
Constraint: MTZ subtour elimination: for each pair of distinct customers and each vehicle, if vehicle v travels directly from customer c1 to c2, then the visit position of c2 must be at least one more than c1's position, preventing subtours

Title: Call Center Shift Scheduling
Keywords: binary variable, scalar parameter
Description: A call center must staff a set of daily shifts using a pool of available employees. Each shift requires a minimum number of workers on duty to handle expected call volume. Each employee has a known cost associated with working each particular shift — reflecting overtime rates, preferences, or seniority differentials. No employee should work more than a specified maximum number of shifts per week to comply with labor regulations. Determine the minimum-cost schedule that assigns employees to shifts such that all minimum staffing requirements are met and no employee exceeds their weekly shift limit.
Objective: minimize
Objective description: Total labor cost across all employee-shift assignments where an employee is scheduled to work
Decision variables: work[e,s]: 1 if employee e is scheduled to work shift s, 0 otherwise (binary)
Parameters: shift_cost[e,s]: cost of scheduling employee e to work shift s; min_coverage[s]: minimum number of employees required on shift s; max_shifts_per_employee: maximum number of shifts any employee may work per week
Constraint: For each shift, the total number of employees scheduled to work that shift must meet or exceed the minimum required staffing level
Constraint: For each employee, the total number of shifts they are scheduled to work must not exceed the maximum allowed shifts per week

Title: Workforce Upskilling Planning
Keywords: binary variable, ordered set, temporal lag (inequality), skill accumulation, 3D variable
Description: A company trains workers over 4 quarters to acquire skills needed for upcoming projects. Once a worker gains a skill, they retain it. Training capacity limits how many workers can be trained per quarter. Skill supply (skilled workers) must meet demand each quarter. Minimize total training cost.
Objective: minimize
Objective description: Total training cost = sum over workers, skills, quarters of training_cost[w,sk] * train[w,sk,q]
Decision variables: train[Workers, Skills, Quarters]: 1 if worker w is trained in skill sk in quarter q (binary); skilled[Workers, Skills, Quarters]: 1 if worker w has skill sk by end of quarter q (binary)
Parameters: training_cost[Workers, Skills]: cost to train worker w in skill sk; skill_demand[Skills, Quarters]: number of workers needed with skill sk in quarter q; training_cap[Quarters]: maximum total trainings per quarter
Constraint: Skill accumulation: once skilled, a worker retains the skill (temporal lag - skills cannot decrease)
Constraint: Train to skill: training in a quarter makes the worker skilled that quarter
Constraint: Skill demand met: number of skilled workers per skill per quarter must meet demand
Constraint: Training capacity: total trainings per quarter cannot exceed capacity
